description: TrueX-Space is a 5-member team of B.Tech CSE (Artificial Intelligence) undergraduates from Amal Jyothi College of Engineering, Kanjirappally, Kerala. Located in the Western Ghats foothills, we fuse AI, remote sensing, and edge-IoT to tackle monsoon disasters. For Dancing with the SARs, we are building SAR-HydroTwin—a physics-informed digital twin combining cloud-penetrating SAR radar backscatter data (NASA-ISRO NISAR) with ground river telemetry for flash-flood early warning.
summary:
SAR-HydroTwin is an interactive, physics-informed geospatial digital twin built for the Dancing with the SARs challenge. Optical Earth-observation satellites are blinded by thick monsoon cloud cover precisely when flash floods and landslides strike mountainous regions like Kerala’s Western Ghats. While Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) from missions like NASA-ISRO NISAR penetrates clouds to detect standing water and soil moisture shifts, satellites experience multi-day revisit gaps.

SAR-HydroTwin bridges this gap by combining dual-polarization L-band/C-band SAR backscatter physics ($\sigma^0$ dB specular reflection drop and cross-polarization volume-scattering ratios) with Digital Elevation Model (DEM) slope masking to eliminate mountain radar-shadow false positives. We fuse these orbital inundation masks with real-time ground telemetry from simulated ESP32 ultrasonic river-level nodes via a hybrid machine-learning fusion engine. Users can interactively explore before-and-after SAR backscatter maps, inspect polarization drivers, and simulate real-time flash-flood alerts across the Meenachil and Pamba river basins.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

SAR-HydroTwin is an interactive web-based radar remote sensing and early-warning platform designed to track monsoon surface-water inundation, soil moisture saturation, and terrain instability in cloud-covered regions.

  1. Physics-Driven SAR Backscatter Engine: Smooth standing floodwater acts as a specular reflector, bouncing radar pulses away from the satellite and causing a sharp drop in co-polarized backscatter intensity ($\sigma^0_{HH}$ / $\sigma^0_{VV}$ in dB). Simultaneously, saturated soils and flooded vegetation alter cross-polarized ($\sigma^0_{HV}$ / $\sigma^0_{VH}$) volume scattering. Our Python processing pipeline applies adaptive Otsu thresholding and log-ratio change detection across multi-temporal SAR scenes to isolate inundation and soil-moisture anomalies.
  2. Topographic Radar-Shadow Correction (DEM Masking): In steep terrains like the Western Ghats (Kanjirappally/Kottayam region), radar layover and mountain shadows mimic low-backscatter water signatures. We integrate NASA SRTM Digital Elevation Model (DEM) slope derivatives to mask out slopes $>15^\circ$, drastically reducing false-positive flood classifications.
  3. Orbital-to-Ground AI Sensor Fusion: Because orbital SAR passes occur on multi-day cycles, our hybrid Gradient-Boosted / Physics-Informed fusion model combines baseline SAR inundation maps with high-frequency ground river-gauge telemetry (modeled on ESP32 + JSN-SR04T ultrasonic sensor nodes) to interpolate basin-wide flood spread and forecast 6-hour flash-flood risk during satellite revisit gaps.
  4. Interactive Storytelling & Visualization: The web interface features a synchronized Before/After SAR swipe comparator, polarization toggle (HH vs. HV vs. RGB Composite), physical driver annotations, and live basin telemetry gauges.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Core Processing & AI: Python 3.11, NumPy, SciPy, Scikit-Image (Otsu thresholding & morphological filtering), Scikit-Learn (spatio-temporal risk fusion), Rasterio / GeoPandas.
  • Interactive Frontend: Streamlit / React + Leaflet (Folium) with custom HTML/CSS before-and-after SAR imagery sliders and Plotly telemetry charts.
  • Edge Telemetry Architecture: Simulated MQTT/JSON telemetry streams modeled after ESP32 microcontrollers and JSN-SR04T waterproof ultrasonic level sensors.

Uniqueness, Creativity & Key Design Factors

Rather than treating SAR imagery as static pictures or relying on generic AI wrappers, SAR-HydroTwin embeds radar wave-surface interaction physics directly into its classification pipeline. By pairing local lived experience in Kerala’s monsoon-prone Western Ghats foothills with NASA-ISRO NISAR’s L-band vegetation-penetrating capabilities, our system demonstrates how orbital radar and low-cost ground sensors work together to protect vulnerable communities.
